statements.statement: The school committee's chosen spending scenario for reallocated state aid totals $418,000
Finance committee voted unanimously to recommend approval of Article 1 as written, $418,056
The final FY27 state budget signed in July gave Lunenburg several hundred thousand dollars more in state aid than the Governor's January budget assumed
The original spending plan had marked $129,458 for Ignite tutoring seats; that money was freed up for reallocation after the district got a smaller grant
Town and school leadership agreed to fund $5,541 of Article 1 with school choice credits and backfill that amount into the Article 3 ask, pending School Committee ratification
A finance committee member said Lunenburg students are currently receiving $800,000 less in services than they did in FY26
A finance committee member said the school budget remains $375,000 away from last year's level-service funding
School Committee set the Article 3 cost to restore middle school sports and some high school sports, with transportation, at $45,849
Net of the $5,541 school choice offset, the working Article 3 target is roughly $40,308
Superintendent said the school committee does not plan to pursue its own Proposition 2½ override and will instead cut elsewhere if funding is not available next year
A member said funding Article 3 even up to $150,000 from special stabilization funds would not put the town in financial peril given current reserves
Superintendent said three newly identified out-of-district special education placements average about $156,000 each with transportation
